page: Amazon Web Services m6i.16xlarge is a general-purpose, hypervisor-managed instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, delivering 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs via two threads per core. The configuration includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-assisted cryptography instructions, such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, are supported alongside vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance features a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities. Multi-core evaluations such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU score within the upper quartile, reflected in solid results for parallelized tasks including Clang compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In application-focused metrics, the instance achieves high static web serving throughput exceeding 46 GB/sec and strong database operation performance. However, single-core execution metrics—such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core—remain within mid-tier percentiles. Similarly, DDR4 memory bandwidth scales reliably for large uncached blocks but tests within average levels compared to more modern memory standards.

From an infrastructure perspective, the absence of integrated local NVMe storage means workloads rely entirely on network-attached volumes, making external I/O architecture an important consideration for disk-intensive services. Nevertheless, the dense allocation of 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, backed by dedicated Nitro CPU assignment, provides high compute density. The platform is well-matched for scalable enterprise applications, including static and dynamic web serving fleets, parallel code compilation pipelines, distributed caching nodes, enterprise relational databases, and multi-threaded batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Configured with 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs, it pairs 256 GB of DDR4 memory with a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets, but does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight upper-quartile multi-core compute capability, static web serving throughput, and database transaction performance, alongside mid-tier single-threaded scores. Lacking local disks, the system depends on network storage for persistence. Its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio makes it suitable for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, relational database engines, and parallel backend data processing workloads.
